content: Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can increase the risk of a heart rhythm condition known as QT prolongation. This risk may be heightened if you are taking certain medications, such as diuretics (commonly referred to as water pills), or if you experience conditions like severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. Clarithromycin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if absolutely necessary, as it passes into breast milk and may affect a nursing infant. Drug interactions can alter the way your medications work or increase the likelihood of serious side effects. It is important to maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications can affect how clarithromycin is removed from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Similarly, clarithromycin can slow the removal of other drugs from your body, which may impact their function. If someone overdoses on this medication and exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. This medication has been prescribed specifically for your current condition and should not be used for other purposes. While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as cultures or liver and kidney function tests, to monitor your progress. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Clarithromycin is used to treat a variety of bacterial infections. It may also be combined with anti-ulcer medications to treat certain types of stomach ulcers or used to prevent specific bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as macrolide antibiotics and works only against bacterial infections. It is not effective for viral infections, such as the common cold or flu. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually every 12 hours. For optimal results, take it at evenly spaced intervals. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. If you are using this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication too early may result in a return of the infection. If you are taking it to prevent an infection, follow your doctor’s instructions carefully and do not stop without their approval. Common side effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, and changes in taste. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition may occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Before taking clarithromycin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics (such as erythromycin or azithromycin), or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Clarithromycin may cause a condition that affects the heart rhythm (QT prolongation). The risk of QT prolongation may increase if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low potassium or magnesium levels in the blood can also increase this risk, especially if you are taking diuretics or experiencing severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
